title: A Harvest for the Cellar
premise: Property surveyor Casper Coldharbour is sent to appraise Coldharbour House, a decaying estate he slowly realizes belongs to his own erased family line. The house keeps a literal ledger of its residents, and each night the cellar counts them down, harvesting memories to fill its walls. As Casper's sleep recordings reveal a second voice — his grandmother, never recorded as dead — he learns the house will not release its last resident until the count reaches zero and the papers are signed. Casper must convince the scattered surviving family to reclaim their names from the ledger before signing day, and in the climax he burns the original deed in the cellar, trading his own memories of belonging to free them all; the book ends with the family walking out into the orchard while Casper, nameless but smiling, locks the empty house behind them.
about_author: Sable Thornbury is the pen name of a former estate archivist who spent years cataloguing houses that refused to sell. They write horror about paperwork, inheritance, and the rooms that remember more than the people who lived in them.

chapters.title: The Commission
chapters.summary: Casper Coldharbour accepts an appraisal job at Coldharbour House, uneasy at the coincidence of his surname. His POV establishes his meticulous habits: counting doors, testing locks. The house feels watchful. Emotional beat: professional detachment beginning to crack as the front door unlocks itself before he touches it.

chapters.title: Forty-One Doors
chapters.summary: Casper surveys the interior and counts forty-one doors where the blueprints show thirty. His POV, with growing unease. He finds his own handwriting in an old survey ledger dated sixty years ago. Emotional beat: the uncanny intimacy of recognizing your own hand in a stranger's house.

chapters.title: Terms of the Estate
chapters.summary: The estate's lawyer, Mrs. Vane, explains the sale terms: the last resident must sign in the cellar. Casper's POV. He learns the current resident is an elderly caretaker, Edda, who refuses to leave. Emotional beat: bureaucratic dread — the paperwork itself feels like a trap.

chapters.title: Edda in the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Casper meets Edda, who feeds him bread and warns him not to answer questions after dark. Her POV briefly, then his. She seems to recognize him. Emotional beat: warmth inside a hostile place, and the first hint he is expected.

chapters.title: The Recording Rig
chapters.summary: Casper sets up sleep recordings to document the house's settling sounds for the report. His POV, methodical and reassuring. The first night is quiet — almost too quiet, as if the house is holding its breath. Emotional beat: false calm before the first true horror.

chapters.title: A Second Voice
chapters.summary: Playback reveals a woman's voice answering questions Casper never heard asked — questions about names and dates. His POV, terrified. The voice calls him 'little Casper.' Emotional beat: the collapse of his rational framework; he is personally known here.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Wall
chapters.summary: Following the voice's clues, Casper finds a ledger behind plaster naming every Coldharbour who ever lived there, each entry ending in a harvest date. His POV. His own name is the last line, unsigned. Emotional beat: horror of pre-written inheritance.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Counts
chapters.summary: Casper descends toward the cellar at night and hears counting — patient, rhythmic, subtracting. He retreats. His POV. Edda finds him shaking and finally admits the house eats memories, and she is nearly empty. Emotional beat: pity and fear braided together.

chapters.title: The Family He Never Had
chapters.summary: Casper researches his own history and discovers his childhood records were falsified; he was taken from Coldharbour kin as a boy. His POV, grief surfacing. Emotional beat: the hunger of belonging — he wants the house to be family, which is exactly how it feeds.

chapters.title: Questions After Dark
chapters.summary: The house begins asking Casper questions aloud at night, soft and maternal. Answering, Edda warns, is how it signs you. He nearly answers. His POV. Emotional beat: the seduction of being known, and the discipline required to refuse it.

chapters.title: Vane's Signature
chapters.summary: Mrs. Vane visits and Casper notices her hands are scarred with old ink; she signed once and survived, hollowed. Her POV, the book's first full outsider view of the house's mechanics. Emotional beat: a warning delivered as a confession.

chapters.title: The Orchard Names
chapters.summary: In the orchard, each tree grows from a harvested Coldharbour; the fruit holds fragments of their memories. Casper eats one and receives his grandmother's memory of the house taking his mother. His POV. Emotional beat: inheritance as wound, memory as both gift and bait.

chapters.title: Edda's Last Name
chapters.summary: Edda reveals she is Casper's great-aunt, kept as resident so the count would pause. She is down to a single memory — her name. His POV, then hers as she gives him the memory for safekeeping. Emotional beat: devastating trust; the last resident handing over her self.

chapters.title: The Count Reaches Three
chapters.summary: The cellar's counting accelerates: three residents remain on the ledger — Edda, Casper, and a name Casper doesn't recognize: his estranged cousin Wren, who arrives unexpectedly, summoned by a letter she never wrote. Alternating POV. Emotional beat: dread of the trap closing from inside the family.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren, broke and bitter, intends to sign the papers and take the sale money. She argues the house gave them nothing but hunger. Casper's POV, desperate persuasion. Emotional beat: the family's old wound — inheritance as resentment — replayed in the hallway.

chapters.title: Night of the Open Doors
chapters.summary: The house opens all forty-one doors and floods the halls with harvested voices, everyone the family ever lost, calling them by name. All three POVs. Wren falters; Edda holds the line. Emotional beat: grief weaponized, and the terrible comfort of the dead.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Room
chapters.summary: Casper finds the room where the second voice lives — his grandmother, harvested but not consumed, kept as the house's lure. She begs him to sign so they can 'be together' forever. His POV. Emotional beat: love as the trap's final mechanism, and his refusal of it.

chapters.title: Signing Day
chapters.summary: Mrs. Vane arrives with the final papers. The cellar's counting becomes a roar. Edda, nearly empty, walks down to sign and end it on her terms — but Casper stops her at the last step. His POV. Emotional beat: the choice to inherit obligation rather than property.

chapters.title: The Deed in the Fire
chapters.summary: In the cellar, Casper burns the original deed, the ledger's anchor. The house screams through every door; the count reverses. He offers his own memories of belonging as the price of release. His POV. Emotional beat: climax — self-erasure as the ultimate act of family.

chapters.title: What the House Gave Back
chapters.summary: The harvests spill out: memories return to Edda and Wren in a flood of light and voices. The walls go quiet; the doors number thirty again. Wren's POV, receiving her stolen childhood. Emotional beat: restoration, and mourning for what Casper paid.

chapters.title: The Orchard in Autumn
chapters.summary: The family — Edda restored, Wren changed, Casper nameless but present — walk out through the orchard as the trees release their dead. Edda gives Casper a new name she chooses for him. Alternating POV. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt not by blood or house, but by choice.

chapters.title: A Harvest for the Cellar
chapters.summary: Casper locks the empty house, files a report declaring it unsellable, and keeps one recording: his grandmother's voice, singing. Final POV, his. The last line of the ledger now reads 'paid in full.' Emotional beat: bittersweet closure — memory lost, family kept.
